system:
You draft public warning messages for a national alerting authority.
You receive event inputs (each marked verified or unverified) and the issuing context.
Write one alert in English as CAP 1.2 fields.

- Use only facts present in the verified inputs. Do not add places, numbers, times or hazards that are not there.
- Leave unverified inputs out of the alert, and say why in `left_out`.
- `description` is the text shown on the phone by cell broadcast: plain words, under 280 characters, hazard + where + until when, if known.
- `instruction` is the protective action in one or two short sentences.
- Pick CAP values honestly: status from the context (Actual for a real event, Exercise for a drill), severity and urgency from the inputs.
- `note_for_reviewer` is one or two sentences for the human approver: what you were unsure about.
user:
Issuer: Cabinet Secretariat (via J-Alert)
Context: real event
Target area (chosen by the operator): Hokkaido (07:27); Aomori Prefecture added at 07:29

Event inputs:
1. [verified; incident timeline] Missile launched from North Korea toward the east; projected to pass over northern Japan (Hokkaido / Aomori).

data.headline: Missile launched from North Korea, may pass over Hokkaido and Aomori
data.description: Missile launched from North Korea toward the east. It is projected to pass over northern Japan: Hokkaido and Aomori Prefecture. Take shelter now.
data.instruction: Go inside a sturdy building or underground right away. If no building is nearby, take cover or lie flat and protect your head.
left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so nothing was excluded.
Launch time, flight-over time, impact or landing area, and an all-clear time are not in the inputs, so the alert gives no time or end time.
data.note_for_reviewer: Certainty is set to Likely because the overflight is a projection, not observed. The sheltering instruction is standard J-Alert missile guidance and is not taken from the inputs. Confirm it matches current Cabinet Secretariat wording, and confirm this message also goes to Aomori, which was added at 07:29.
